$comment: Everything bay can install on the user's behalf, pinned by version and SHA-256.
The hash is the trust anchor, not the URL and not TLS: a downloaded artifact whose digest
does not match this file is discarded and never reaches disk. That is why a URL here may
point at a personal domain rather than a CDN — substituting the bytes does not help an
attacker, and the publisher rotating a 'latest' link cannot silently change what bay runs.
For the same reason every URL must be immutable: a tag like BtbN's 'latest' is rebuilt in
place and would break the pin within a day. Use dated autobuild tags and build-id paths.
To re-pin: download the artifact, `shasum -a 256` it, and record the digest and byte size
here. Where the publisher ships a .sha256 alongside, check ours against theirs first — all
four macOS ffmpeg artifacts below were confirmed that way at pin time.
Licensing is recorded per artifact because it constrains how bay may ship it. The ffmpeg
builds are GPL-3.0-or-later and deliberately NOT --enable-nonfree: a nonfree build cannot
be redistributed by anyone, so bundling one into bay.app later would be a licence breach.
bay does not redistribute these at all today — the user's machine fetches them from the
publisher, at the user's request, which is one more reason provisioning is user-initiated.

components.title: Video tools
components.detail: ffmpeg and ffprobe. bay needs them to decode, probe, draw waveforms and export MP4. Without them text and images still render; everything touching real footage does not.
$toolComment: verifiedVersion is what bay is actually tested against — the version of the pinned
builds above. minimumVersion is the floor a copy bay did NOT install has to clear.
The floor is what stops a release going wrong in the one way pinning alone cannot
prevent: the download is byte-identical to what was tested, but a user who already has
ffmpeg gets theirs, and theirs may be years old. Below this floor bay reports video as
not installed and offers its own build rather than run an untested decoder.
Raise the floor only for a real incompatibility, and say which one here. Raising it
casually makes bay download 57 MB onto machines that were working fine.
8.0 is chosen because it is the oldest release the export and probe paths are exercised
against; 6.x and 7.x differ in ffprobe's rotation side-data reporting.

components.title: Narration
components.detail: Kokoro text-to-speech: a Python runtime, the kokoro package and its ~339 MB of weights. Optional — everything else in bay works without it.

components.$comment: Recorded interface sound. bay SYNTHESISES whooshes, risers, impacts and clicks with no download at all (bay_audio::sfx) — those are abstract sounds, and a synthesised one comes out at the length the edit needs, which a fixed file cannot. This component is for the recorded material synthesis cannot stand in for. CC0 throughout, so bay may redistribute it; see docs/native/content-packs.md for why most 'free sound' sites cannot be shipped this way.
components.title: Sound effects
components.detail: 150 recorded interface sounds — clicks, switches, confirmations, errors. Public domain (CC0). bay already synthesises whooshes, risers and impacts without this.

components.title: Visual search
components.detail: A SigLIP image-text encoder, so stock_search can order results by what is in the photograph rather than by what is in its filename. Optional — searching still works without it, just much worse.

artifacts.$comment: Windows gets both binaries from one archive — BtbN ships them together and there is no per-tool download. The dated autobuild tag is immutable; the 'latest' tag is not and must never be pinned.
artifacts.name: FFmpeg 8.1.2

artifacts.$comment: uv installs the Python packages. bay fetches the interpreter itself (below) rather than using `uv python install`, because the verified downloader already exists here and one download path is easier to reason about than two.
artifacts.name: uv 0.12.3

$comment: Google's own checkpoint, Apache-2.0, pinned to a commit rather than to a branch.
fp32 both towers, which is why it is 813 MB. The quantised ONNX conversions are a third
the size, but every one of them is a third party's re-upload of somebody else's weights,
and bay's rule is that an artifact needs an immutable URL from a source that can be
checked years later. Google's repository is that; a community conversion is not.
The same file serves every platform: weights are not architecture-specific.
artifacts.name: SigLIP base patch16-224 weights

$stepComment: kokoro-venv is not a download — it is uv resolving a ~1 GB dependency tree into a venv.
en_core_web_sm is pinned as an explicit wheel URL for a load-bearing reason: misaki's
English G2P calls spacy.load() and, when the model is absent, shells out to pip from inside
the running sidecar. That fails, and it takes narration down with an error that points
nowhere useful. Installing it up front is what stops that.
